ESSENCE: [0] Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.

paragraphs.text: Each holy thing is defined by what drops out of it. A sacred word counts when you stop hearing its letters. A holy gesture counts when every bodily straining has melted away. The practice counts when even the flow of breath is used up.
And then the payoff: for people wise enough to reach that place, everything — absolutely everything — turns out to be wonderful. That is the festival.

paragraphs.text: Mantra is what remains when letters drop out. Mudra is what remains when effort drops out. Yoga is what remains when breath drops out. Each holy thing is defined by its vanishing.
Then the punchline: for those who get there, everything is wonderful. All of it. That is the celebration.
